Donation credited mostly to the elementary, primary and middle schools.

decisions.decision: Chair proposed, and both sides agreed, to expand the student-government appeal hearing from the agenda's 5 minutes to 15 minutes per side.
Committee will take the student-government election appeal under advisement and issue a written decision, aiming for early the following week.
The student-council nomination form has already been changed for next year to avoid the signature-line discrepancy.

Committee will hold off on changing the fifth-grade bus-release consent procedure until the superintendent returns and new legal counsel weighs in, and will invite parents to a future meeting to discuss it.
A proposal to let families donate to cover other students' field trip costs will be added to the agenda for the next policy discussion.

public_comment.topic: Thanked Lunenburg teachers for teacher appreciation week and thanked residents who attended town meeting and voted for the override; noted the May 16th election and early voting.
Shout-out to the Lunenburg PTO, noting funds raised for the schools and open board positions, with a June meeting announced.
Appeal of the superintendent's denial of his challenge to the student-council election's 14-signature nomination standard, arguing the printed rule required 15 signatures.
public_comment.stated_role: junior at Lunenburg High School, candidate for class president

public_comment.topic: Advocated for his son's appeal, arguing the principal exceeded statutory authority and the superintendent's process denied due process.
Explained that student council meetings are open to the public and that John Bowen Jr. had been permitted to attend some of them.
Said he believed the election was fair because the missing signature line was a typo that affected all candidates equally.

minutes.summary: The committee handled routine business (minutes, line-item transfers, donations, a superintendent's report read in her absence, a facilities update, and two grant approvals) before spending roughly ninety minutes on a formal hearing over a disqualification/appeal dispute in the class-of-2027 student council election, ultimately taking no vote and reserving a written decision. It closed with an inconclusive discussion of whether to loosen the fifth-grade school-bus release consent rule, deferred pending the superintendent's return and new legal counsel.

what_happened.line: Committee heard roughly 90 minutes of testimony on an appeal over a disputed student-council election and took no vote, reserving a written decision.
Members approved a batch of year-end line-item transfers, including moves among substitute-teacher lines and a special education paraprofessional account.
Committee voted to authorize applying for a federal literacy grant, capped at an amount as heard, and for FY27 DESE entitlement grants.
Discussion of loosening the fifth-grade school-bus release consent rule was deferred until the superintendent returns and new legal counsel weighs in.
Committee waived second reading on four policies covering cash handling, student data privacy, medication administration, and school advertising.

why_it_matters: The written decision on the election appeal will set how the district resolves nomination-signature disputes in student government going forward.
Year-end transfers show which school programs, including substitute teaching and special education paraprofessional support, ran short of their budgeted lines.
Any change to fifth-grade bus-release rules affects how parents authorize after-school pickup, and now waits on new legal review before moving forward.
watch_next: Written decision on the student-council election appeal, expected early the following week
Future meeting inviting parents to discuss the fifth-grade bus-release consent procedure

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.coverage: official minutes are a summary only
reconciliation.summary: The official minutes are essentially the meeting agenda with an attendance block and an adjournment line — they record almost no vote outcomes, no transfer amounts, and no decision detail, so nearly every substantive item in our minutes is "only in ours" rather than a true conflict. The two exceptions worth checking are the $745,084.51 warrant total, which appears only in the official minutes and nowhere in our transcript-based record, and the "Second read Policies" agenda language, which is worth reconciling against our minutes' claim that the second reading was waived.
